transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Rivera (CTO, Maplewood), Dr. Elena Park (Head of AI), Mike Chen (Platform Engineer)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're going to run through how Redwood handles rate limits, org and project keys, and the console controls. Priya will do a quick live walkthrough of the console and API.
[00:18] Sam: great, we appreciate it. quick context — Maplewood is multi-tenant, we have about ~120 clinics, and we need per-tenant quotas and isolation.
[00:30] Jordan: perfect. one of the main things we'll show is the difference between org-level controls and project-level keys, so you can enforce company-wide limits or give projects separate quotas.
[00:45] Priya: i'll share my screen — can everyone see the Redwood Console? (brief pause) yes?
[00:55] Dr. Park: yes, we can see it. the font on the deck is small, but it's fine.
[01:10] Priya: cool. so on the left nav we have Projects, Org settings and Rate Limits. at the org level you can set global quotas and default policies; then each project (which maps to a tenant or app) can have override quotas and its own API key.
[01:30] Mike: so project keys are the ones we'd give to each clinic? and we can cap them individually?
[01:36] Priya: exactly. you can create project keys per clinic, set token-per-minute and monthly token quotas, and also set hard vs soft limits. soft limits will throttles with warnings; hard limits will 429.
[01:54] Sam: what's the enforcement point — edge, gateway, or inside the inference runtime? we need something that's reliable if a single clinic spikes.
[02:05] Priya: enforcement happens at the request router layer before hitting GPU runtime; so it prevents wasteful tokens. we also have burst windows and a token-bucket implementation. small imperfections: the console labels say "rate-limt" in one spot (autogen typo) but functionally it's enforced at the edge.
[02:30] Dr. Park: can you do a demo where a clinic exceeds its quota and another uses shared capacity?
[02:38] Priya: yep — i'm going to create a test project called "maplewood-demo-clinic-77". creating key... ok key created. note: i'm using a demo org that has a default monthly cap of 10M tokens and per-key minute cap of 1000.
[03:00] Priya: i'm going to use a local script to hammer it — you'll see the requests start to 429 once the per-minute cap hits.
[03:12] (sound of typing)
[03:20] Priya: ok you can see in the console live metrics there — requests/min, token consumption, and the recent 429 rate. also showing the policy that triggered: project_key_rate_limit.
[03:36] Mike: and is there an alerting hook? we'd want Slack or PagerDuty when a tenant hits >90% of quota.
[03:44] Priya: yes, under Alerts you can add webhook integrations (Slack, PagerDuty, Datadog). you can also create an alert rule by metric percent-of-quota. we'll attach a sample Slack webhook in the follow-up.
[03:58] Jordan: just to clarify on billing — usage is still tracked at org and project granularity so you can invoice tenants or absorb cost.
[04:10] Sam: okay good. what about burst capacity — some clinics have sudden spikes during telehealth rush, can we allow bursts without permanently raising their quota?
[04:22] Priya: we have a burst buffer and a priority routing mode. you can set a burst allowance (x tokens per burst window) and a fallback policy: either queue (if low-latency tolerant), degrade to smaller model or route to a cheaper variant, or reject.
[04:40] Dr. Park: degrade to smaller model — is that automatic or manual? we can't accept quality regressions for certain flows (diagnosis assistant), but for summaries we can degrade.
[04:53] Priya: it's policy-driven. you can tag endpoints/prompts as "high-quality" vs "best-effort". for best-effort we can automatically fallback to a smaller open model. for high-quality we honor the hard limits or route to dedicated capacity if available.
[05:08] Mike: how does dedicated capacity fit in? if we lease Redwood Dedicated, does the org-level quota still apply?
[05:16] Jordan: good question — dedicated pools are capacity-backed. you get a committed throughput and you can configure routing policies: prioritize dedicated for production tenants and fallback to hosted for overflow. quotas still exist so you can prevent runaway usage even within Dedicated.
[05:32] Priya: also note dedicated gives lower variance on latency — helpful for clinical real-time workflows.
[05:40] Sam: security — we need SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS key control. do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:48] Priya: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations; you can bring-your-own KMS. audit logs show key rotations, access events, and admin changes. SSO via SAML/OIDC with SCIM for provisioning is supported. i'll share the SOC 2 + ISO paperwork after this call.
[06:05] Dr. Park: nice. is data residency configurable per org? some clinics are in different states with different requirements.
[06:12] Jordan: we have region routing policies — you can pin projects to regions. for stricter requirements, our Private deployment offers VPC/on-prem option.
[06:22] Sam: for a pilot we'd want hosted, but with audit logs and KMS — sounds fine.
[06:27] Priya: next i'll show the API example: POST /v1/generate with header X-Redwood-Project-Key. sample curl in the UI shows the header usage. (reads out) if a key hits its rate limit you'll get 429 with a Retry-After header and a structured error explaining quota usage.
[06:50] Mike: is there a way to aggregate limits — e.g., allow per-operator plus per-clinic? we have internal users that make calls on behalf of multiple clinics.
[06:59] Priya: we support labels/metadata on requests. you can enforce nested policies: global org cap, project cap, and a sub-key or operator cap. the enforcement evaluates highest precedence rule. it's in the docs — we'll send the policy priority matrix.
[07:18] (brief pause)
[07:25] Sam: are there CSV exports for usage? our billing team needs per-clinic daily usage.
[07:31] Priya: yes, under Reports you can export per-project daily breakdowns and configure S3 delivery. also the Cost & Usage API can stream usage to your billing system.
[07:42] Dr. Park: great. any integration limitations with common API gateways? we run Kong and AWS ALB.
[07:50] Priya: we provide a sidecar & ingress configs and an upstream proxy guide for Kong, and ALB is supported via header forwarding. we'll include the Kong example in the follow-up.
[08:02] Jordan: quick objection we often hear — why not just implement at our own gateway? Redwood reduces operational burden, per-token efficiency (KV cache, prefix caching) and gives consistent model fallbacks.
[08:16] Sam: cost — we have to compare that to just fronting calls ourselves.
[08:20] Jordan: fair. we usually recommend a short benchmark and cost model run: we'll simulate your traffic and show per-token and per-request costs with and without caching.
[08:30] Priya: speaking of benchmarks, if we run a 1-hour benchmark with your prompt set, we can show realistic latency numbers and cost savings from caching/quantization.
[08:40] Mike: okay. what does setup look like for project keys? can we rotate them? we need rotation every 90 days.
[08:47] Priya: keys can be rotated automatically; we support key aliases and seamless rotation with zero downtime if you configure the new key in parallel. audit logs show rotations.
[08:58] Sam: what about per-tenant SAML? like each clinic has its own SAML?
[09:04] Jordan: usually customers use org-level SSO and then projects are provisioned via SCIM. per-tenant SAML is supported in Private deployments where each tenant gets a separate control plane.
[09:18] Dr. Park: can we tag specific prompt types so we can have different enforcement for PHI-containing flows?
[09:25] Priya: yes you can tag endpoints and create policy sets. for PHI, you can route to Private with extra isolation, and require customer-managed KMS. also you can add masking or PII scrubbing in the request pipeline.
[09:40] Mike: latency under load — any numbers? p95 at 1k reqs/min?
[09:46] Priya: depends on model and seq length; for our medium-sized models p95 at steady-state on shared hosted is ~250-350ms for a 512 token response; under bursting it can increase, which is where dedicated helps. we'll include model-specific latency profiles in the follow-up.
[10:04] Sam: okay. can you show the console place where we create org-level default policies?
[10:10] Priya: sure — Org settings -> Default Policies. here's a sample policy: monthly_org_cap: 10000000 tokens; default_project_min: 10000; project_overrides_allowed: true. you can also enforce tags to prevent accidental overrides.
[10:28] (screen scroll)
[10:35] Priya: one more demo — i'm going to simulate two projects: one hitting 95% of monthly quota sends alert; the other spikes and gets burst allowance then fallback to smaller model.
[10:50] (typing)
[11:00] Priya: alert sent to Slack (simulated). visible in notifications pane.
[11:08] Dr. Park: when fallback happens, do we get a trace showing which fallback decision was made? that's critical for troubleshooting.
[11:15] Priya: yes, tracing shows the routing decision, the policy that matched, and the model variant chosen. traces are available in the Console for 90 days under Trace Explorer or pushed to your APM.
[11:30] Mike: what about rate-limits for embeddings? we do a lot of vector indexing — do token quotas apply or do you have separate units?
[11:39] Priya: embeddings are metered by vector units + request rate; you can set separate quotas and rate-limits for embedding endpoints.
[11:47] Sam: excellent. anything around per-minute vs per-second granularity? sometimes we need sub-minute throttling for bursty flows.
[11:56] Priya: we support per-second, per-minute, per-hour windows. sub-minute enforcement is available at the edge.
[12:05] Jordan: ok wrapping up — recommended pilot: 1) issue project keys for 5 clinics, 2) run 1-hour benchmark with prompts, 3) evaluate alerts and billing export.
[12:18] Sam: timeline — we'd like the pilot next week if possible. Mike can provide traffic samples today.
[12:24] Mike: yes i'll upload traffic profile and a sample prompt set by EOD.
[12:29] Dr. Park: please include the rules for fallback so our product team can review.
[12:34] Jordan: we'll send pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, Kong/ALB examples, and the benchmark playbook.
[12:40] Priya: action items noted. any other questions?
[12:44] Sam: not from me. thanks — that was useful.
[12:48] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the links and schedule the bench.
[12:52] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and a small OCR-like typo in the console label were left to mimic auto-transcript noise. References: Slide deck "rate-limits-deck.pdf" (shared), Docs link: https://redwood.ai/security-soc2 (shared in chat), Kong example gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kong-proxy-example (to be shared).
